alex: Heads-up: planning a small change in Python/TS SDKs — default batching window reduced from 50ms -> 20ms to cut tail latency.
alex: Side-effect: with routed policies and fallback variants we've seen quota attribution jump in console per-route because SDKs now flush smaller batches more often.
tariq: Wait — can you sketch how quota is getting attributed today?
alex: Today we attribute tokens to whichever route is on the request at final dispatch. If a request falls back to a cheaper model the SDK still reported the original route header in most cases, but with the smaller batches we get more granular flushes and some requests split across routes which the console aggregates as separate hits.
carmen: Saw this in canary: per-route token graphs show a sawtooth pattern and totals > actual tokens observed at infra level. snippet from logs:
```
[ingest] route=prio-A tokens=120
[ingest] route=fallback-B tokens=30
[infra] gpu_tokens=140
```
jenna: Is this a breaking change for customers? Will older SDK versions see different quotas?
mike: It can be surprising. Two paths: change server-side attribution (coalesce by request id/original route) or add an opt-in SDK header with canonical route metadata so ingestion can stitch events.
alex: Proposal: SDKs add `X-RW-ROUTE-ORIG: <route-id>` (opt-in env var `RW_ROUTE_CANONICAL=1` initially). Also send `X-RW-BATCH-SEQ` so we can group flushes. Example: 
```
headers = {
  'Authorization': 'Bearer ...',
  'X-RW-ROUTE-ORIG': 'tenant-A:prio',
  'X-RW-BATCH-SEQ': 'abcd-1234'
}
```
deploy-bot: canary: sdk-py v1.9.0-canary deployed to us-west-2 at 2026-03-18T14:02Z :rocket:
tariq: If we add headers, does the telemetry pipeline already surface them? Console needs per-route aggregation to prefer `X-RW-ROUTE-ORIG` when present.
carmen: I can add a lightweight transform in ingestion to prefer `X-RW-ROUTE-ORIG` and merge `X-RW-BATCH-SEQ` grouped events for last-30s windows. Fallback: if no header, keep current logic.
jenna: Rolling plan? My suggestion: 1) SDK opt-in canary (1.9.0-canary), 2) ingestion transform behind a feature-flag, 3) surface new header in console with a note, 4) after 2 weeks flip default on in SDK.
mike: Agree. Also make sure quota billing uses infra-side canonical tokens for billing, console shows attributed view. 
alex: I'll open a PR in both python and ts sdks with env opt-in + docs. Tagging @devex for SDK docs and @product for console messaging.
ej: +1 :thumbsup: (not in thread, sent separately)
jenna: One more ask — add telemetry metric `rw.batch.flush_size` so we can monitor the change impact on token granularity.
carmen: will add metric and a dashboard tile (dev only) to track per-route divergences.
alex: Cool. I'll prepare release notes that call out "opt-in header for canonical routing and batch grouping" and include migration steps.
mike: Thanks. If anyone sees weird spikes post-canary ping me in #release-war-room.
jenna: Sounds good. :+1:
